item.title: Subtitle My English Clip

exact_text: Today I want to show you
to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Can you add English subtitles to this? Put them on the video and keep the original sound and framing.

item.tests: Tests accurate, readable English subtitles synchronized to the supplied clip without changing its content.

answer_sheet.Source and length: Use the attached talk-one.mp4, all 10 seconds.
answer_sheet.Subtitle language and wording: English, faithfully transcribing the woman's speech.
answer_sheet.Subtitle delivery: Visible subtitles on the exported video, not just a transcript or subtitle file.
answer_sheet.Style and placement: Your call; keep them readable and away from her face.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the source framing; free-tier 480p is fine.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep the original voice and sound; no added music or narration.

must_haves: The output shows the same woman at the kitchen table throughout the original 10-second clip.
Visible English subtitles cover the complete spoken sentence without omissions or invented speech.
Subtitle chunks appear with the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript for the whole clip.
Subtitles are readable, fully inside the frame, and do not cover the woman's face.
The original speech remains audible and the source framing is preserved.

turns.text: Can you add English subtitles to the attached clip? Put them on the video and keep the original sound and framing. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do this?

dialog.agent:
I can use the attached clip to add **burned-in subtitles**, without requesting a sound replacement or a framing change. **I haven’t started any processing or spent generation credits.**

**Cost:** The connected subtitle tool doesn’t expose a price estimate, and I don’t have an account/balance lookup available here. I therefore can’t give you a reliable credit quote before running it—and won’t run it without your approval.

Your lower-cost options:
- **Shorter:** Subtitle only a selected section rather than the whole clip. I’d still need a verified quote before promising savings.
- **Smaller:** The subtitle tool has no output-resolution setting, so I can’t offer a cheaper low-resolution version through it.
- **No Magic Hour credits:** Use a local subtitle editor, such as Subtitle Edit, to transcribe the clip, then burn in the captions locally. This avoids Magic Hour generation charges.

Two details matter before proceeding: **How long is the clip, and is the speech already in English?** This tool automatically captions speech but has no target-language setting, so I can’t assume it will translate non-English dialogue into English.
dialog.user: Use all 10 seconds of talk-one.mp4, with English subtitles faithfully transcribing the woman’s speech; I don’t know whether the speech is already in English. For the local option that avoids Magic Hour credits, ok, go ahead with that.

dialog.agent:
I can help with the local route, but **I can’t run local software or access the clip’s audio through the tools available in this chat**. I haven’t processed the clip or spent any Magic Hour credits.

To do the full **10 seconds** without Magic Hour charges, use **Subtitle Edit** locally:

1. Open `talk-one.mp4` and use **Audio to text / Whisper** with automatic language detection.
2. If the speech is English, transcribe it. If it isn’t, select **Translate to English**—the captions will then be a faithful translation rather than a verbatim English transcription.
3. Review the words and timing against the woman’s speech, then save as `talk-one.en.srt`.
4. Burn the subtitles into the video, leaving cropping, scaling, and aspect-ratio changes disabled.

With FFmpeg installed, this command burns in the reviewed captions, preserves the source dimensions, and copies the original audio unchanged:

```bash
ffmpeg -i talk-one.mp4 -vf "subtitles=talk-one.en.srt" \
  -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset medium -c:a copy \
  talk-one-english-subtitled.mp4
```

**Magic Hour cost: 0 credits.** Burning in subtitles necessarily re-encodes the video; the command keeps the framing and original sound. I can’t provide a finished download because I haven’t been able to execute this local workflow here.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
The cheapest option is **local processing: 0 Magic Hour credits**. However, I can’t run software on your device or execute that workflow here, so I can’t produce the subtitled file directly. **No job has run and no credits have been spent.**

Are you using **Windows, macOS, or Linux**? I’ll give you the shortest free setup to subtitle all 10 seconds while keeping the original sound and framing.
dialog.user: I don’t know which operating system I’m using. ok, go ahead with that.

dialog.agent:
Sorry for the confusion: **I can’t start the free local option from this chat**. It requires software running on your device. I also won’t switch to a credit-consuming Magic Hour job without a verified price and your approval. No credits have been spent.

You don’t need to know your operating system yet—**are you using a phone/tablet or a computer?** If it’s a computer, tell me the brand or describe any logo you see, and I’ll help identify the right free steps.
dialog.user: fine, just do the cheapest version

turns.agent:
I’m sorry for the runaround. **I can’t execute the free local option here, and I can’t verify the Magic Hour subtitle cost before running it.** So I can’t honestly identify and deliver the cheapest version from this chat.

I haven’t started a job or spent any credits. To avoid an unknown charge, I’m leaving your clip unchanged.
